club: Maples Tech Club (MTC) — Learn it. Build it. Ship it.

questions.question_text: In a document editor, which shortcut makes selected text Italic (slanted)?
In a document editor, which shortcut UNDERLINES the selected words?
What is the difference between the Backspace key and the Delete key while typing?
questions.option_a: Backspace erases to the left of the cursor; Delete erases to the right of the cursor
questions.option_b: Both do the exact same thing

questions.question_text: If you want to quickly FIND a specific word on a long webpage or PDF, which shortcut do you press?
Which key at the top-left of the keyboard is commonly pressed to cancel a pop-up or exit full-screen video?
Which function key is the classic shortcut to REFRESH or reload a webpage in a browser?
If you pressed Ctrl + Z (Undo) by mistake and want your change back, which shortcut performs REDO?
Which keyboard shortcut lets you quickly switch between open apps/windows on Windows?
To type a single capital letter or the "@" symbol above the number 2 without turning on Caps Lock, which key do you hold?
Which shortcut opens a brand-new blank document or window in most apps?
In a web browser like Chrome or Edge, what does pressing Ctrl + T do?
In a web browser, what does pressing Ctrl + W do?
Which key on a Windows keyboard is used to capture a screenshot of your entire screen?
When a file or folder is selected on Windows, pressing which function key lets you RENAME it immediately?
What does pressing Alt + F4 do on a Windows computer?
questions.option_c: Closes the currently active app or window

questions.question_text: In a browser, pressing Ctrl and the "+" (plus) key together does what?
questions.option_b: Zooms in to make text and images appear larger

questions.question_text: After zooming in on a webpage, pressing Ctrl + 0 (zero) does what?
questions.option_d: Resets the page zoom back to normal (100%)

questions.question_text: When filling out an online form (like Name, Roll No, Class), pressing the Tab key usually does what?
questions.option_b: Moves the cursor neatly to the next input box

questions.question_text: On a smartphone or tablet, the screen both shows pictures AND senses your finger taps. What is it called?
What Does "Hardware" mean in simple everyday words?
questions.option_a: The physical parts of a computer that you can actually see and touch

questions.question_text: In Indian homes and school labs, a small box called a UPS is connected to desktop PCs. Why is it useful?
questions.option_d: It provides short battery backup during a power cut so you can save your work safely

questions.question_text: What is the opposite of a Printer — a device that turns a paper certificate or drawing into a digital image file on your PC?
Which single modern cable carries BOTH sharp high-definition video AND audio from a laptop to a TV or projector?
At a supermarket checkout or school library, which handheld device reads black-and-white striped labels instantly?
Why can a laptop keep running during a power cut even without an external UPS?
questions.option_b: Laptops have a built-in rechargeable battery inside

questions.question_text: What is the tiny removable storage card used inside many cameras and Android phones called?
What is the main job of the small spinning fan inside a laptop or desktop cabinet?
questions.option_a: To blow dust onto the screen
questions.option_b: To keep the processor and internal parts cool so the computer does not overheat

questions.question_text: In everyday phones and computers, what is the simple difference between RAM and Storage (SSD/ROM)?
questions.option_a: RAM stores photos forever; Storage deletes everything on restart
questions.option_b: RAM holds active apps temporarily while working; Storage keeps your photos and files saved even when powered off
questions.option_d: Both are names for the screen

questions.question_text: If your computer opens 15 browser tabs and starts feeling sluggish when switching apps, having more of which part helps most?
Modern laptops use an SSD instead of an older spinning Hard Disk (HDD). What everyday benefit do you notice right away?
questions.option_b: You never need to charge the battery
questions.option_d: The laptop boots up and opens apps much faster, with no moving disk parts

questions.question_text: Which newer oval-shaped reversible charging/data port is found on almost all modern Android phones and newer laptops?
What do we call the main circuit board inside a computer that connects the processor, RAM, storage, and ports together?
If a wireless mouse stops moving the cursor on screen, what is the FIRST simple hardware thing you should check?
questions.option_b: Check if its battery is low or its tiny power switch underneath is turned OFF

questions.question_text: A pen-like tool used by digital artists and students to write or draw neatly on a tablet screen is called a:
Which storage capacity is LARGER when comparing a pendrive or laptop storage?
Roughly how many Gigabytes (GB) make 1 Terabyte (TB) on a hard drive?
Which popular design app/website lets students easily create posters, certificates, and invitations using ready templates?
What does "Software" mean in simple everyday language?
questions.option_b: The power socket on the wall
questions.option_c: Soft cloth used to clean a monitor
questions.option_d: The apps, programs, and operating system that run inside a computer or phone

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an Operating System (the core system software that runs a PC or phone)?
Why do schools send circulars and admit cards as a ".pdf" file instead of an editable Word file?
questions.option_c: PDFs do not take even 1 byte of space
questions.option_d: PDFs keep the exact layout, fonts, and alignment looking identical on every phone and computer

questions.question_text: Which application is best suited for keeping an attendance list, marks table, or club budget with automatic totals?
What is the difference between "Copy & Paste" and "Cut & Paste" on a file?
questions.option_c: Copy leaves the original file in place and makes a duplicate; Cut moves the file to the new folder

questions.question_text: What is a ".zip" file commonly used for when sharing a project?
questions.option_a: Bundling many files/folders together into one smaller compressed file for easy sending

questions.question_text: In Word or Google Docs, what is the difference between "Save" and "Save As"?
questions.option_a: "Save" updates the current file; "Save As" lets you save a separate copy with a new name or location
questions.option_d: Both print the document on paper

questions.question_text: Which long bar at the bottom of a Windows screen shows the Start button, pinned apps, and clock?
Why do many students turn on "Dark Mode" in apps when reading or working in the evening?
questions.option_b: It prints pages in black paper
questions.option_c: It uses a dark background that feels gentler on the eyes in low light
questions.option_d: It makes Wi-Fi twice as fast

questions.question_text: If you want to jot down a quick plain-text note with zero heavy formatting, which lightweight built-in Windows app opens instantly?
When saving an image with a transparent background (such as a school logo), which image format supports transparency cleanly?
On Windows, files ending in ".exe" (or ".apk" on Android) are what kind of files?
questions.option_b: Application installer / executable program files (only run from trusted official sources!)

questions.question_text: Before editing an important project presentation, why is naming files clearly like "Science_Poster_v2_Final.pptx" better than "asdf123.pptx"?
questions.option_b: Computers refuse to save short names
questions.option_c: Clear file names let you and your teammates find the right version in seconds without confusion

questions.question_text: What does the "Spell Check" wavy red underline in Word or Google Docs indicate?
questions.option_a: A word that may have a spelling typo so you can review and fix it
questions.option_b: That the sentence will be deleted automatically
questions.option_d: That the computer has a virus

questions.question_text: If a single app stops responding ("Not Responding") on Windows, how can you close JUST that stuck app without unplugging the whole PC?
questions.option_a: Open Task Manager, select the frozen app, and click "End Task"
questions.option_b: Pull the electric plug from the wall

questions.question_text: What is "Open-Source Software" (such as Linux, VLC, Blender, or LibreOffice)?
questions.option_a: Software that leaves your computer unlocked to strangers
questions.option_b: Software whose source code is openly shared so anyone can use, study, and improve it legally
questions.option_d: Software that works only for 1 hour

questions.question_text: When you install a new PDF app and Windows asks which "Default App" should open .pdf files, what does that setting control?
questions.option_c: Which program opens automatically whenever you double-click any .pdf file

questions.question_text: Which of these is ALSO a popular web browser besides Google Chrome?
questions.option_c: Mozilla Firefox / Microsoft Edge / Apple Safari

questions.question_text: If you visited a helpful website yesterday and forgot its name, which browser list helps you find it again?
What is the real difference between Google Chrome and Google Search?
questions.option_a: Chrome is a search website; Google is a laptop brand
questions.option_d: Chrome is the Browser app installed on your device; Google Search is a website used inside a browser to look up info

questions.question_text: When you see `https://` and a padlock icon in the browser address bar before logging in, what does the "s" in `https` mean?
questions.option_b: Secure — data between your browser and the website is encrypted so others on Wi-Fi cannot read your password

questions.question_text: What does opening an "Incognito" or "Private" browser window ACTUALLY do on a shared computer?
questions.option_a: It blocks all computer viruses automatically
questions.option_b: It makes you completely invisible to websites and your internet provider
questions.option_c: It stops the browser from saving your browsing history, cookies, and login session on THAT computer after you close the window
questions.option_d: It gives free unlimited mobile data

questions.question_text: If a webpage shows "404 — Page Not Found", what does that simply mean?
questions.option_a: The specific link or page was moved, deleted, or typed with a spelling mistake

questions.question_text: When writing a polite email to a teacher or competition organizer, why should you always fill in the "Subject" line?
questions.option_a: So the receiver immediately knows what your email is about before even opening it
questions.option_b: Emails cannot be sent without 50 words in Subject
questions.option_c: Subject is where you type your password

questions.question_text: If an expected registration confirmation email has not arrived in your Inbox, which email folder should you check next?
Why do websites sometimes ask you to tick "I am not a robot" or pick traffic lights (CAPTCHA)?
questions.option_c: To stop automated spam bots from creating fake accounts or flooding forms
questions.option_d: To test your eyesight for driving

questions.question_text: In Chrome or Edge, which shortcut opens your recent Downloads list directly inside the browser?
What are website "Cookies" in everyday browsing?
questions.option_d: Tiny text files saved by websites in your browser to remember things like your login status or dark-mode preference

questions.question_text: In Google Search, putting quotation marks around an exact phrase like `"Maples Academy Khatauli"` helps you find:
questions.option_a: Pages that do NOT mention Maples Academy
questions.option_b: Pages containing that exact phrase with those words together in that order

questions.question_text: What is Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive an example of?
questions.option_b: A physical pendrive inside your pocket
questions.option_c: Cloud storage — lets you save files online and open or share them from any phone or computer

questions.question_text: When sharing a Google Drive project link with your teacher, why should you check whether access is set to "Restricted" vs "Anyone with the link can View"?
questions.option_a: If left "Restricted", your teacher will see "Access Denied" when clicking your submitted link!
questions.option_b: View access lets anyone delete your account

questions.question_text: On a noisy browser tab playing unexpected music, what does the tiny speaker icon on that tab let you see or do?
questions.option_a: Spot immediately which tab is playing sound and even mute that tab

questions.question_text: What does an email ending in `.edu.in`, `.ac.in`, or `.gov.in` in India tell you about the website/sender?
questions.option_a: Anyone can buy it anonymously for ₹10 without verification
questions.option_b: It belongs to a verified Indian educational institution (`.edu.in`/`.ac.in`) or government body (`.gov.in`)

questions.question_text: If you start writing an email in Gmail and close the tab before clicking Send, where is your unfinished message saved automatically?
What is a "Browser Extension" (or Add-on)?
questions.option_d: A small optional helper tool added inside your browser (which you should install ONLY from trusted creators)

questions.question_text: When a YouTube video pauses with a spinning circle in the middle because the internet is slow, what is that called?
Roughly how far does normal Bluetooth (like wireless earbuds connected to your phone) usually reach clearly?
questions.option_d: A short room-size distance (around 10 meters / 30 feet)

questions.question_text: Your laptop says "Connected to Wi-Fi, No Internet." What does this message actually mean?
questions.option_b: Your laptop is connected to the Wi-Fi router in the room, but the router’s outside internet line is down
questions.option_c: Your laptop Wi-Fi card is broken

questions.question_text: Why are desktop computers in an exam lab often connected by Ethernet (LAN) cables instead of Wi-Fi?
questions.option_b: Desktop PCs can never use Wi-Fi
questions.option_c: A wired Ethernet cable gives steadier, interference-free internet for 30+ PCs at the same time
questions.option_d: LAN cables also power the monitor without electricity

questions.question_text: Internet plan speeds from providers like JioFiber, Airtel, or BSNL are commonly advertised in "100 Mbps". What does Mbps measure?
questions.option_a: Megabits per second — how fast data transfers over your internet connection
questions.option_c: How far the Wi-Fi reaches in meters
questions.option_d: How many months the plan lasts

questions.question_text: Companies like BSNL, Airtel, Jio, or local fiber broadband providers that connect homes/schools to the internet are called:
Why does Wi-Fi signal become weaker when you walk three rooms away behind thick concrete walls?
questions.option_b: Thick walls and distance absorb and weaken wireless radio waves from the router

questions.question_text: What is a "Local Area Network (LAN)" in simple everyday words?
questions.option_c: Computers, laptops, and printers connected together inside one building, home, or school campus

questions.question_text: If ONE Wi-Fi printer is connected to the school office Wi-Fi router, how many computers on that same Wi-Fi can print to it?
questions.option_a: Only phones with no SIM card
questions.option_b: Only a computer plugged into it with an HDMI cable
questions.option_d: All authorized computers/phones on that same Wi-Fi network can share and print to it wirelessly

questions.question_text: When you mirror your phone or laptop screen wirelessly onto a classroom Smart TV without any cable, what is that feature called?
Every device connected to a network gets an identifying number address (like a house number for delivering data packets). What is it called?
You are using a 1.5 GB/day mobile data pack via Hotspot. Watching 2 hours of video at `4K / 2160p` vs `480p` will do what?
questions.option_c: `4K` uses many times more mobile data and can finish your 1.5 GB pack very quickly!

questions.question_text: On a laptop connected to someone’s mobile Hotspot, turning ON "Metered Connection" (or Data Saver) helps because:
questions.option_a: It pauses huge background Windows updates so your friend’s mobile data does not drain suddenly

questions.question_text: On modern dual-band home Wi-Fi routers, you often see two Wi-Fi names: `Home_2.4G` and `Home_5G`. What is the practical difference?
questions.option_a: `5 GHz` gives faster speeds nearby in the same room; `2.4 GHz` reaches farther through walls
questions.option_b: `5G` Wi-Fi requires a 5G SIM card inside the router
questions.option_d: There is no difference at all

questions.question_text: What is "Quick Share / Nearby Share / AirDrop" on modern phones and laptops used for?
questions.option_a: Charging another phone from 10 meters away
questions.option_b: Sending photos or project files fast between two nearby devices wirelessly without wasting internet data

questions.question_text: Why should you avoid logging into banking or sensitive accounts on an open, password-free public Wi-Fi at a railway station or café?
questions.option_a: Public Wi-Fi breaks your phone camera
questions.option_c: Unsecured open Wi-Fi networks make it easier for attackers nearby to snoop on traffic or set up fake twin hotspots

questions.question_text: In online video calls or multiplayer games, what does "High Ping / High Latency" (e.g., 450 ms instead of 25 ms) feel like?
questions.option_d: A noticeable delay or lag between clicking/speaking and getting a response back

questions.question_text: What brings ultrahigh-speed broadband into modern schools and homes using hair-thin strands of glass carrying pulses of light?
When you use a diagram, photo, or quote created by someone else in your school presentation, what is the honest thing to do?
questions.option_a: Crop out their name and claim it as yours
questions.option_b: Forbid anyone else from seeing the source
questions.option_d: Give clear credit to the original creator or source instead of pretending you made it yourself

questions.question_text: To keep your eyes comfortable while studying or working on a computer, what does the healthy "20-20-20 Rule" recommend?
questions.option_b: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds to relax your eyes
questions.option_c: Sit 20 millimeters from the screen for 20 hours

questions.question_text: Important UPI Safety Rule in India: Do you EVER need to enter your secret UPI PIN to RECEIVE money from someone?
questions.option_a: UPI PIN is just your roll number
questions.option_b: Yes, you must enter UPI PIN to receive gifts
questions.option_c: NEVER! A UPI PIN is ONLY entered when money is GOING OUT from your account — asking you to enter PIN to "receive" money is a scam!
questions.option_d: Yes, scanning any QR code automatically credits money after PIN

questions.question_text: What is "Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)" on email or social accounts, and why is it great?
questions.option_a: It adds a second check (like a code on your phone) besides your password, so thieves can’t break in with a leaked password alone
questions.option_b: It slows down typing speed by half
questions.option_c: It deletes your account after two days
questions.option_d: It forces two friends to share one account

questions.question_text: Why is reusing the EXACT SAME password across 10 different games, websites, and your main email risky?
questions.option_a: If even one small game site gets hacked, attackers immediately try that same password on your email and other accounts!
questions.option_c: It uses extra storage on your phone

questions.question_text: How should a responsible student use AI tools (like ChatGPT or Gemini) when working on a project or assignment?
questions.option_a: Copy-paste the entire AI output without reading a word and sign it as 100% your own
questions.option_b: Use AI to brainstorm, understand tough ideas, or debug — then write/build in your own understanding and honestly mention where AI helped
questions.option_d: Trust every single date or quote from AI without checking

questions.question_text: You install a simple "Flashlight" app on a phone, and it suddenly asks permission to read your Contacts, Call Logs, and Messages. What should you think?
questions.option_a: Flashlights need your contacts to shine brighter
questions.option_c: Deny/uninstall! A flashlight only needs the camera LED — asking for private contacts and messages is a big privacy red flag

questions.question_text: What is "Phishing"?
questions.option_d: Fake emails, SMS, or look-alike websites pretending to be a trusted bank/company to trick you into typing passwords or OTPs

questions.question_text: What does your "Digital Footprint" mean?
questions.option_a: Walking barefoot in the computer lab
questions.option_c: The size of your laptop in inches
questions.option_d: The lasting trail of posts, comments, photos, and public activity associated with you on the internet

questions.question_text: Why is downloading "Cracked / Pirated" paid software or game cheats from shady websites dangerous as well as unethical?
questions.option_b: Besides disrespecting creators’ work, pirated cracks are one of the #1 ways password-stealing malware infects home PCs!
questions.option_c: Cracked software runs faster and safer than official apps
questions.option_d: Official free alternatives like VLC, GIMP, or LibreOffice do not exist

questions.question_text: Before clicking "Save Password" when Chrome asks on a shared school or cyber-café computer, what should you ALWAYS choose?
questions.option_a: Share it with the café owner
questions.option_b: Click "Save" so you never have to type again
questions.option_c: Click "Never" — saving your password on a shared computer lets the next person log straight into your account!
questions.option_d: Write your password on a sticky note on the monitor

questions.question_text: In a class study WhatsApp/Telegram group, what keeps the group helpful and respectful for everyone?
questions.option_a: Keeping messages relevant, polite, avoiding late-night spam chains, and respecting classmates’ opinions
questions.option_b: Starting personal arguments in front of 60 people
questions.option_d: Sending 80 stickers in a row at midnight

questions.question_text: Why do phones and Windows regularly release "Security Updates"?
questions.option_a: To patch newly discovered security holes so hackers and malware cannot exploit them

questions.question_text: If a classmate accidentally left their Gmail open on a school lab computer, what is the ONLY ethical thing to do?
questions.option_a: Read their private emails for fun
questions.option_b: Immediately click "Sign Out" without reading a single email, and politely let them know to be careful next time
questions.option_d: Send a prank email from their account

questions.question_text: Sometimes AI chatbots confidently make up a fake book title, date, or fact that sounds very believable. What should you do before putting AI facts into a school project?
questions.option_c: Verify important facts, dates, and quotes from a reliable textbook or trusted official website
questions.option_d: Assume computers can never be wrong

questions.question_text: Why is keeping phones on silent and putting screens away at least 30–45 minutes before sleep recommended by doctors?
questions.option_d: Bright late-night screens and endless notifications disturb deep sleep and leave you tired in class the next morning

questions.question_text: If you receive an uncomfortable, threatening, or scam message from an unknown account online, what 3 steps protect you best?
questions.option_a: Send them your phone number to argue back
questions.option_c: Keep it secret and worry alone
questions.option_d: Do NOT reply or argue — take a screenshot as proof if needed, Block/Report the account, and tell a trusted parent or teacher

questions.question_text: What is "Plagiarism" in school projects and digital work?
questions.option_b: Copying someone else’s article, code, or artwork and presenting it as your own original work without credit
questions.option_c: Saving a backup copy on a pendrive
